kind.content: A small kitchen with a long memory.
Fifteen years of early bread, day-boat fish and neighbours who became regulars.

kind.alt: Head chef Nadia plating a dish in the open kitchen

kind.content: It started with one oven and a borrowed espresso machine.
Tidewater began as a bakery counter in the old net loft, feeding fishermen at six in the morning. The bread got a following, then the soup, then someone asked if we might stay open for dinner.
Fifteen years on we are still on the quay, still baking at dawn, and still buying from the same boats and the same three farms up the valley. The room got bigger. The idea did not.
Cooks like her grandmother, plates like a jeweller.
Pulls the first shot at 7:40 every morning.
Knows your name by the second visit.

kind.alt: Head chef plating a dish in the open kitchen

kind.content: “They remember how I take my coffee and my daughter's name. It is the closest thing this town has to a living room.”
Breakfast, lunch or a slow dinner. There is almost always room at the bar.
Seasonal plates, slow coffee and a long table by the water. Family-run since 2011.
© 2026 Tidewater Kitchen. Made with care in Port Ellery.
